title: Balanced Binary Tree
prompt:
Return whether a binary tree is **height-balanced**: for every node, its two subtrees' heights differ by at most 1.

**Example**: `[3,9,20,null,null,15,7]` → `true`; `[1,2,2,3,3,null,null,4,4]` → `false`.

Compute heights bottom-up, using a sentinel `-1` to signal 'already unbalanced' so you don't recompute.
hints: Checking balance at a node needs both subtree heights. Can a single pass compute heights and detect imbalance at the same time?
Write a helper that returns a subtree's height, or -1 if anything below is unbalanced. If either child returns -1, return -1 immediately.
If `Math.abs(l - r) > 1`, return -1; otherwise return `1 + Math.max(l, r)`. The tree is balanced exactly when `helper(root) != -1`.

solution.explanation: Using -1 as a "poison" height packs two facts into one return value (template (c)), so one post-order pass both measures heights and detects imbalance. Calling a separate `height()` at every node would cost O(n²). O(n) time, O(h) stack.
